correctness.rationale: Solving the initially empty first-order channel gives Q_j=jλ∫e^(−jλ(T−t))c(t)dt. Under y=e^(−λ(T−t)), Q_j/j is the (j−1)st moment of the measure with density c(T+log(y)/λ) on [e^(−λT),1]. With mass Q1, its normalized third central moment is Δ/(4Q1³). A single rectangle gives one uniform interval, so the contrast vanishes. For twins the earlier and later transformed intervals have lengths zL and L (L=x(1−r)), center difference D=x(1+r)(1−z)/2, and normalized weights a=z/(1+z), b=1/(1+z). The third central moment after centering the two uniform populations is abD[(a−b)D²+(L²−z²L²)/4]. This yields exactly the boxed factorization; one factor r−z distinguishes strict separation from contiguity with the stated sign. At x=r=1/2,z=1/4,C=1 the exact ratios give u+v=51/80 and uv=163/3200, so the stated u,v,C' match the first three moments of the twin. Since 36<sqrt(1297)<37, the endpoint v exceeds 1/16 and u<1; both histories fit the same deployment and the twin contrast is −189/1048576. The lower bound is for the first three rates in the prescribed progression, not a tested assertion about arbitrary sensor designs. The gap-dependent positive factor has strictly negative second log derivative and opposite infinite first log derivatives at z=0,r. It therefore has exactly one unconstrained interior maximum, with a finite deployment truncating the gap interval as stated. All discrimination is exact and promise-dependent; small signals may not be reliably distinguishable under error.

value.rationale: Temporal integration loses information, so the distinction between within-class recovery and one-versus-two discrimination matters. A signed fourth measurement separates the two physical classes under the exact promise in spite of exact ambiguity at three, with an explicit positive-gap interval where contrast grows and then declines. This is a structural identification boundary, not general moment algebra alone. The result neither quantifies real-world error nor promises calibrated equal-step clearances or a useful noise threshold.
